channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Open New Jalal-Abad International Airport in Fall 2027
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to expand air cargo capacity with a new international airport in Jalal-Abad and a cargo terminal near Bishkek, set to open in fall 2027. The project, costing an estimated $60 million, includes a 3,600-meter runway and a passenger terminal. It aims to handle international flights and serve as a cargo hub, potentially linked to the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Sold Resort Linked to Sanctioned Russian Entity, Investigation Claims
item.description: An investigation by OCCRP alleges that the Kyrgyz government sold the 'Bars' resort on Issyk-Kul, previously seized from crime boss Kamchy Kolbaev, to an entity financed by a sanctioned Russian organization. While President Sadyr Japarov stated the resort was sold for $12 million, twice its estimated value, documents suggest it was sold for approximately 60% of its initial valuation, with no significant funds entering the state budget.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Sadyr Japarov Applies for Second Term in 2027 Election
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov has submitted his application to run for a second term in the upcoming presidential election scheduled for January 27, 2027. Since assuming power in October 2020, Kyrgyzstan has transitioned to a presidential system, experienced economic growth, and seen several prominent figures face legal challenges.

item.title: Nearly 100,000 Kazakh Citizens Declared Bankrupt, Debts Totaling Hundreds of Billions of Tenge
item.description: According to the Committee of State Revenues, 98,600 Kazakh citizens have been declared bankrupt, with their debts amounting to 373 billion tenge. Currently, 23,000 more citizens are undergoing bankruptcy proceedings, with total debts of 134.5 billion tenge. The personal bankruptcy law was introduced in Kazakhstan in March 2023.

item.title: Kazakhstan requires 3 GW of flexible power capacity
item.description: Kazakhstan has a need for 3 gigawatts (GW) of flexible power generation capacity. This indicates a requirement for power sources that can quickly adjust output to meet fluctuating demand, crucial for grid stability.

item.title: UN Women: Women and girls disproportionately bear the cost of the climate crisis
item.description: UN Women reports that women and girls bear a disproportionate burden of the climate crisis. A 1-degree Celsius rise in global temperature could lead to a 34% greater loss of income for women compared to men. The organization urges gender equality to be central to climate actions.

item.title: Quality Maintenance Ensures Reliability of Uzbekistan's Energy System
item.description: Reliable operation of the energy system depends on quality maintenance, timely provision of equipment, and efficient operations. President Mirziyoyev emphasized expanding local production of spare parts and developing service capabilities during a visit to NURA Electric.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Cut Mobile Device Customs Duty to 0% Upon WTO Accession
item.description: Uzbekistan will reduce the customs duty on imported mobile devices to 0% upon its accession to the World Trade Organization (WTO). This move is expected to make mobile devices up to 5% cheaper for consumers, though VAT will still apply. Negotiations are ongoing since 1994.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Allocate 103.7 Million Euros for Climate Change Adaptation
item.description: Uzbekistan will allocate 103.7 million euros to adapt to climate change. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev participated in the opening ceremony of the COP31 summit in Antalya, where climate change mitigation and adaptation to water scarcity and global warming were discussed. A regional program for Central Asia was launched.

item.title: Turkmenistan Authorities Reportedly Refuse Military ID for Students Educated Abroad
item.description: Young Turkmen citizens who studied abroad and returned home are reportedly being denied military ID cards by conscription offices. Sources suggest this is a punitive measure for avoiding military service by studying overseas. The military ID is crucial for employment and other essential life functions in Turkmenistan.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Average cost of market trading places analyzed
item.description: In Q3 2026, the average daily cost for a market trading spot in Kyrgyzstan was 225.16 soms for daily markets and 111.95 soms for Sunday markets, according to the National Statistical Committee. Bishkek had the highest average cost for daily markets at 336.07 soms.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Several science organization heads resign after audit
item.description: Following a state audit of science funding in Kazakhstan, several officials have resigned. These include the heads of the Science Institute, the National Scientific and Technical Information Center, and the Science Fund. Over 51 billion tenge in violations were identified, with 37.7 billion tenge recovered.

item.title: US Sanctions Tajik National for Alleged Role in Iran's Missile Procurement Efforts
item.description: The United States has sanctioned Alisher Domullodzhanov, a Tajik national, for his alleged involvement in Iran's efforts to acquire man-portable air-defense systems (MANPADS). The sanctions, imposed under Executive Order 13949, target individuals involved in Iran's arms trade.

item.title: Russia and Ukraine Agree on Large-Scale Prisoner Exchange
item.description: Russia and Ukraine have reached an agreement on a large-scale exchange of prisoners. The details of the agreement were not immediately disclosed, but it signifies a potential step towards de-escalation between the two nations.

item.title: Taliban Disperse Protest Over Pakistani Medicine Ban in Kandahar
item.description: Sources reported that Taliban forces dispersed a protest by pharmaceutical company employees in Kandahar against a ban on Pakistani medicines. The protest began in Jadeh-e Naw, with demonstrators demanding alternatives. Taliban forces surrounded the area, preventing further demonstrations.

item.title: Jayhun Residents Protest Home Demolitions Amidst Unfulfilled Promises
item.description: Residents of Gulrez village in Jayhun district are protesting the demolition of their homes, built on land legally acquired five years ago. Videos show a woman shielding her house from bulldozers. Villagers claim authorities encouraged construction and promised a school, but are now forcing them to leave.

item.title: Araghchi: US Misconceptions Led to Failure of Policy Toward Iran
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that US officials' misconceptions about Iran have caused Washington's policy toward the country to fail. He responded to comments by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, calling them baseless repetitions of remarks made by former Secretary of State Mike Pompeo.

item.title: Uzbekistan Welcomes 11.6 Million Tourists in Jan-Oct, Central Asian Visitors Lead
item.description: Uzbekistan hosted 11.62 million foreign tourists in January-October 2026, a 19.4% increase from the previous year. Citizens from Central Asian countries formed the largest group, with 3.18 million from Kyrgyzstan, 2.7 million from Kazakhstan, and 2.55 million from Tajikistan. Significant numbers also arrived from Russia, Afghanistan, and China.

item.title: Uzbekistan May Abolish Import Duty on Mobile Phones During WTO Accession Talks
item.description: Uzbekistan is considering abolishing import duties on mobile phones as part of its World Trade Organization (WTO) accession negotiations. Agreements on a zero rate have already been reached with other countries. The Customs Committee reported that this could reduce phone prices by nearly 5%, though VAT will remain. Uzbekistan aims to join the WTO by 2026.

item.title: At Least 10 Police Officers Killed in Militant Attack in Pakistan
item.description: At least 10 police officers were killed when militants ambushed a convoy in Pakistan's Kohat district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, on November 11. Among the deceased were two senior officers. The attack occurred in a region bordering Afghanistan. A previous attack in the same district on September 18 resulted in 23 deaths.

item.title: Tashkent Airport Resumes Mobile Phone Customs Clearance After Brief Halt
item.description: Customs clearance for mobile phones at Tashkent International Airport resumed on November 11, less than 24 hours after being temporarily suspended. Specialists from the UzIMEI center will now be permanently present to verify IMEI codes. The suspension was due to increased attempts to illegally import devices with fake IMEI codes.

item.title: UAE-Mediated Russia-Ukraine Talks Conclude, Focus on Prisoner Exchange
item.description: Two-day Russia-Ukraine peace talks, mediated by the UAE in Abu Dhabi, concluded on November 11. Sources indicate an agreement was reached on a large-scale prisoner exchange. Discussions also covered security guarantees, Russia's demands, and the post-war future. The Ukrainian stance prioritizes ending the war before establishing a new European security architecture.

item.title: Tajikistan and Kazakhstan to Cooperate on AI in Energy Sector
item.description: Tajikistan's Ministry of Energy and Water Resources and Kazakhstan's KEGOC have agreed to enhance cooperation in digitalization, artificial intelligence, and energy system management. The agreement was reached during a visit by Tajikistan's minister to KEGOC in Astana, as part of the Tajik president's official visit to Kazakhstan. Discussions focused on digital solutions and AI for improving energy system reliability and efficiency.

item.title: Rosatom to Begin Construction of Two Large Power Units in Uzbekistan in 2027
item.description: Rosatom plans to commence the full-scale construction of two large power units, each with a capacity of 1,000 megawatts, in Uzbekistan by 2027. Currently, work is focused on two small modular reactors of 55 megawatts each. Engineering surveys and design refinements are underway for the larger units, with active work expected to begin next year.

item.title: South Korea Expands Agricultural Technology Support for Uzbekistan
item.description: South Korea is enhancing its support for Uzbekistan's agricultural sector by focusing on rice planting mechanization, dairy cattle breeding, and year-round strawberry cultivation. This initiative aims to boost farm output and conserve water, while also creating new markets for Korean equipment. An agreement signed in September 2026 expands specialist training programs.

item.title: Kazakhstan Develops Legislative Initiatives to Address Rural Personnel Shortage
item.description: A working group of the People's Council of Kazakhstan met to discuss legislative initiatives aimed at resolving the personnel shortage in the agro-industrial complex. Discussions included implementing new educational models through specialized agricultural classes and early career guidance for rural youth.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Tenge Weakens Against US Dollar, Falling to 444.76
item.description: The US dollar exchange rate in Kazakhstan has declined, closing at 444.76 tenge on the Kazakhstan Stock Exchange (KASE). The National Bank's official rate stands at 447.52 tenge. Exchange rates in Astana and Almaty show the dollar being bought at around 443-445 tenge and sold at 447-450 tenge.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's National Bank partners with Crystal Intelligence on blockchain analytics training
item.description: The National Bank of Kyrgyzstan and Crystal Intelligence have signed a memorandum to cooperate on training specialists in virtual assets and blockchain analytics. The agreement facilitates workshops and practical training to analyze virtual asset operations, assess risks, and identify suspicious transactions.

item.title: Kazakhstan may lose $400-470 million due to Russian export restrictions on coal
item.description: Kazakhstan faces potential losses of $400-470 million due to Russia's restrictions on coal exports to Europe via Baltic ports starting in the second half of 2026. Transit volumes have significantly decreased, with Russian Railways not approving transit applications for October and November.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan launches SOS channel for mountain rescue coordination
item.description: Following the tragic death of a teenager in the Ala-Archa gorge, Kyrgyzstan's tourism and mountaineering community has created a Telegram channel named SOS Mountain. The channel aims to improve coordination of search and rescue operations in mountainous areas. It encourages regular mountain visitors to subscribe and share the link.

item.title: Smart Meter Installation Nears Completion in Issyk-Kul Region
item.description: Installation of smart electricity meters for residential subscribers in Kyrgyzstan's Issyk-Kul region is 98% complete. Over 121,000 out of 124,000 subscribers have been equipped with modern meters. The system allows for automatic data transmission and online payment via the 'My Light' app, aiming to improve accuracy and service.

item.title: Kindergarten Director Sentenced to 5 Years for Child's Death in Locked Car
item.description: A private kindergarten director in Uzbekistan's Kashkadarya region has been sentenced to five years in prison for leaving a three-year-old child in a locked car, leading to the child's death from heatstroke. The director failed to check all children after dropping them off. She was also found guilty of embezzlement and document forgery.

item.title: Doctors Report Cessation of Essential HIV/AIDS Medication Supply in Turkmenistan
item.description: Doctors in Turkmenistan's Balkan province report that the supply of essential medications for HIV/AIDS patients has been halted. Anonymous medical professionals stated that the cessation of these drugs, crucial for managing the condition, is leading to a severe deterioration of patients' health. Regional health officials have declined to comment.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Airports Plans Logistics Park, Business Center, and Aviation Museum
item.description: Airports of Kyrgyzstan is developing several projects at Manas International Airport and in Bishkek. Plans include a 15.89-hectare logistics park, an aircraft maintenance hangar, an aviation museum, a 25-story business center with a helipad, and a mosque. Some projects are in the design phase, others are preparing for construction.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Provides Additional Housing for Residents Displaced by Border Clashes
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has provided secondary housing to citizens whose two homes on one plot were rendered unusable during the 2021-2022 border clashes with Tajikistan. The Presidential Envoy's Office in Batken region announced this on November 11. A working group allocated housing transferred from Tajikistan to Kyrgyz territory during border demarcation.

item.title: Iran Produces 50 Missiles Monthly Despite Industrial Setbacks, Western Intelligence Reports
item.description: Western intelligence indicates Iran is producing approximately 50 missiles per month, maintaining half of its pre-war capacity despite US and Israeli strikes. This capability allows the Islamic Republic to retaliate if conflict reignites. The report suggests Iran's industrial sector has overcome significant challenges.

item.title: Kazakhstan Allows Reclaiming Social Benefits After Voluntary Refusal
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Labor and Social Protection clarifies that citizens who voluntarily refuse social benefits can reapply later if their circumstances change. This option is available through the eGov Mobile app. The ministry emphasizes that refusal is a right, not an obligation, and new applications will be reviewed based on current legislation and conditions.

item.title: Bishkek Homeless Shelters Prepare for Winter with Limited Capacity and Uncertain Numbers
item.description: Bishkek has prepared shelter accommodation for up to 150 homeless individuals this winter, with a total capacity of 190 across three facilities. However, updated estimates of the homeless population are unavailable. Challenges in accurately counting the homeless have persisted for years, with figures varying significantly between official and unofficial reports.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Drunk Driver Sentenced to 9.5 Years for Fatal Pedestrian Crash
item.description: A 31-year-old driver in Uzbekistan has been sentenced to 9.5 years in prison for causing a fatal accident while driving under the influence. The driver struck and killed a woman and her two children at a pedestrian crossing in Surxondaryo region. He fled the scene after the incident. One child survived with injuries.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes Eliminating VAT on Potato Exports to Uzbekistan
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has proposed that Uzbekistan eliminate value-added tax (VAT) on potato imports. The proposal was made by the Minister of Water Resources, Agriculture, and Processing Industry, Erlist Akunbekov, during a meeting with his Uzbek counterpart. The discussion also covered establishing a joint venture for agricultural product processing and storage.
